name: Planimetric symmetry
summary: A frame built like a diagram: one central axis, a flat back wall, pastel colour blocks and a camera that tracks or pans at right angles. Every object is placed. The look is a miniature world with a dry joke.

philosophy.core_thesis: A film is a constructed object, so the frame is composed as a flat, symmetrical tableau and the camera moves only at right angles to it.
design_principles: Put the key subject on the vertical axis of the frame and mirror the set about it, so that 90% or more of the visual weight is balanced left to right.
Shoot head-on to the back wall, with the lens axis at 90° to it, and keep the horizon and all verticals true.
Move the camera only on the three right-angle axes: a track along the wall at 0.5 to 1.5 m/s, a pan of 90° or 180° at a steady rate, or a straight push-in over 3 to 6 s.
Limit the palette to 4 to 6 flat colours, one dominant at 40% to 50% of the frame, with the rest in blocks of 5% to 15%.
Stage the actors in a line or a pyramid on one or two planes, facing the lens, and give a deadpan line with no overlap.
Cut at an average shot length of 3 to 5 s and use a whip pan or a title card of 1 to 3 s as a chapter break.
Fix the frame size in advance for each part: 1.37:1, 1.85:1 or 2.39:1, and change it only at a chapter.
anti_patterns: A handheld camera that follows the actor
An off-axis, canted or random angle
A natural, un-graded, muddy colour palette
A cluttered frame with unplaced objects
Shallow depth of field with a blurred background
A lens flare or a bokeh effect for mood

composition.framing: A centred, flat frame: the back wall fills the picture at 90° to the lens, and the set repeats left and right of the axis.
composition.staging_in_depth: 2 to 3 planes parallel to the lens, 1 to 3 m apart: a front prop, the actors on one line and a flat set or wall behind.
composition.subject_placement: On the centre axis, or in a pair about it; the eyes sit on the upper third line and look into or across the lens.

principles.rule: Place the subject on the vertical axis and mirror the set about it, with doors, windows and props in pairs.
Square the lens to the back wall and keep every vertical plumb, so that the frame reads as a flat plan.
principles.value: lens axis at 90° to the wall, 0° tilt

principles.rule: Fill the frame with one dominant flat colour and 3 to 5 accents in small blocks.
Stage the actors on one or two planes parallel to the lens, with a flat wall behind.
Let floor lines, rails and shelves run at right angles to the lens axis, and meet at the central axis.

camera_and_movement.movement: Right-angle moves only: a lateral track along the wall, a 90° or 180° pan, a straight push-in or a pull-out. No handheld follow, no diagonal.
camera_and_movement.support: Dolly on rails, tripod with a fluid head, cable cam for a cross-section shot
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 1.2 to 1.5 m, at the actors' chest and eye level
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Track 0.5 to 1.5 m/s; pan 20° to 40° per second; push-in over 3 to 6 s

lens_and_format.frame_rate: 24 fps; 12 fps or 24 fps stop-motion for the miniature set
lens_and_format.focal_length: 25mm to 40mm (35mm format); a wide lens at a distance for flat planes
lens_and_format.aperture: f/4 to f/8 for deep, even focus across the planes
lens_and_format.resolution: 35mm or 4K digital; a clean, sharp image
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus on all planes; the front prop and the back wall are both sharp.

light.quality: Soft, even and frontal, with a low contrast and a bright fill, as in a storybook illustration.
light.direction: From the front and above, close to the lens axis; no deep shadows on the back wall.
light.colour_temperature: Daylight 5600K or warm tungsten 3200K, with a gel to match the set
light.source: Large soft boxes and bounce at the camera

colour_and_grade.treatment: A pastel, flat palette in blocks. Skin stays warm, blacks are lifted, and one dominant hue colours each chapter.
grade_recipe: Lift the black point to 6% to 8% so that the shadows read as flat colour.
Set the highlights at 92% to 95% and keep a low contrast of −10% with a soft S-curve.
Push saturation of the dominant hue by +20% and mute the other hues by −10%.
Warm the whites to 5200K and add a 3% to 5% pink in the midtones.
Keep grain at 5% to 8%; do not add a vignette or a flare.
colour_and_grade.texture: Fine grain at 5% to 8%, clean flat colour with no digital noise

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 3 to 5 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s for an insert to 12 s for a long lateral track
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut between flat tableaux on the beat of the line. Hold the frame until the joke lands, then whip or cut to the next.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, whip pan of 0.2 to 0.4 s, a title card as a chapter break of 1 to 3 s, an iris in or out.

sound.approach: Clean, close dialogue with exact foley for each prop. Rooms are quiet, and the sound of an object is a gag.
sound.dialogue: Deadpan, a line at a time, with no overlap and a pause of 0.5 to 1 s before the reply.
sound.music: A pop or classical song picked for each chapter, and a harpsichord or marimba theme; each cue starts on a cut.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated, with dialogue peaks at −6 dBFS

titles_and_graphics.treatment: Chapter cards and a narrator's text in a centred block on a flat colour, with an inset or a drawn map as a graphic.
titles_and_graphics.type: A geometric or slab serif in upper case, centred, one colour from the palette; each card stays for 1 to 3 s.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a centred, symmetrical establishing shot of a facade or a room; hold for 3 to 5 s before the first move.

shot_list.shot: Whip pan to the next room

positive: title card in a slab serif

emotion.target_response: Dry, melancholy charm: the viewer sees a small, orderly world in which feeling is held back and shown by arrangement.

use_cases: video prompts for a boutique or a hotel
music video with a built set
avoid_when: The brief needs a documentary or an observed, unplanned moment.
The shot needs a depth of field and a hard, dramatic light.

modifiers.how: Keep the 1.37:1 frame and the deadpan face; leave the set for a street, shoot handheld at eye level and let the passers-by cross the frame.
Keep the symmetry; cut every 1 to 2 s on the beat and add a lateral track on each chorus.

sources.title: Matt Zoller Seitz, The Wes Anderson Collection (Abrams, 2013)
David Bordwell, Figures Traced in Light: On Cinematic Staging (University of California Press, 2005)
David Bordwell, Poetics of Cinema (Routledge, 2008), chapter on staging and planar composition
